# Data formats

All assets live under `src/main/resources/assets/cobblemon_battle_showtime/`. Resource packs can add or override each
kind under their own namespace. Files marked *generated* are rewritten by a script in `tools/`: edit the script, not
the JSON.

## Moves: `moves/<move id>.json` (generated by `tools/moves.py`)

The file name is Cobblemon's move id (`thunderbolt`, `10000000voltthunderbolt`). Only top-level files with at least
one layer are read; subfolders are ignored.

```json
{
  "category": "special",
  "color": "#FFD81A",
  "accent": "#FFFFB0",
  "size": 1.0,
  "layers": [
    { "motif": "sparks_on", "phase": "wind", "duration": 12 },
    { "motif": "bolt", "phase": "travel" },
    { "motif": "burst", "phase": "hit", "particles": ["minecraft:electric_spark"] }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `category` | `physical` (strikes up close, no travel by default), `special`, `status` |
| `color`, `accent` | The move's colours (default: its type's) |
| `size` | Scale of the whole move (Z-Moves: 1.6) |
| `layers[].motif` | A shape from `move/Motifs` |
| `layers[].phase` | `wind` (user winds up), `travel` (user → target), `hit` (from Cobblemon's hit cue), `self` (on the user only) |
| `layers[].delay`, `duration` | Ticks into the phase; length (0 = the phase's) |
| `layers[].color`, `accent`, `size`, `count` | Per-layer overrides; how many blows, rocks, coins… |
| `layers[].block`, `item` | A block or item the motif draws |
| `layers[].particles` | Vanilla particle ids the motif sprays |

`tools/move_data.json` holds every move's data from Cobblemon's battle engine (type, category, flags, target,
boosts…). `moves.py` has three parts: hand-tuned specs, the composer for every other move, and the Z-Moves.
Shadow Ball has no file: it is the `ShadowBall` class.

## Ambiances: `ambiances/<id>.json` (generated by `tools/ambiances.py`)

Top-level blocks, all optional: `time` (`at`, `speed`), `sky` (`sky_color`, `fog_color`, `strength`, `stars`,
`hide_clouds`), `backdrop`, `spotlights`, `floor_lights`, `floating_blocks`, `lightning`, `aurora`, `shooting_stars`,
`rifts`, `rainbow` (`doubled`), `strobe`, `sound`, `ambient_sounds`, `mirror_ball`, `dance_floor`, `neon_grid`,
`sprites`, `critters`, `nebulae`, `galaxy`, `planets`, `mist`, `veins`, `sky_cracks`, `glitch_cubes`, `wisps`,
`ghosts`, `moon`, `flicker`, `bubbles`, `mushrooms`, `film`, `embers`, `volcano`, `caustics`, `shafts`, `kelp`,
`lanterns`, `fireworks` (a moment can also launch `fireworks` over the field; empty `every`: none far off), `glints`,
`fog_wall`, `mirage`, `birds`, `striped_sun`, `palms`, `wormholes`, `islands`, `island`, `court`, `light_towers`,
`crowd`, `followspots`, `confetti_colors` (moments can also open a `wormhole`, throw `confetti`, fire `pyro`, make
the crowd `cheer`, set off `camera_flashes` and play `notes`), a screen `filter` (and `calm_filter`: the filter with calm
effects on, `"none"` to drop it), and `moments` with `send_out`, `attack`, `crit`, `faint`, `victory`, `defeat`
reactions (a moment can also show a big `text`). Spotlights take `alpha`, `ring`, `sector` and `facing`. `ambiance/Ambiance.java` is the reference for every field and its default. Names shown in the
menu come from the lang key `<namespace>.ambiance.<id>` (`cobblemon_battle_showtime.ambiance.<id>` for Showtime's).
`"reserved": true` (1.2.0): shown in the menu and played as the player's own choice only when another mod unlocks it
for them (`ShowtimeHooks.setUnlocks`); imposed on a battle, it plays anyway. Another mod's ambiances live in its own
jar, `assets/<its namespace>/ambiances/`, written by hand.

### Stadiums, presets and props (2026-11-19, `tools/stadiums.py`; the design: [stadiums.md](stadiums.md))

- `stadiums/<id>.json`: the **place**, in the ambiance format: `hide_world`, `cavern` (`rock`, `floor`, `light`,
  `light_strength`, `ambient`, `margin`, `height`, `pillars`, `lava`, `hoard`), `sea` (`sand`, `rock`, `water`, `deep`,
  `foam`, `margin`, `radius`, `wave`, `speed`, `rocks`, `under`, `depth`), `land`, `hall`, `island`, `islands`, `court`,
  `crowd`, `light_towers`, `backdrop`, `galaxy`, `planets`. Combined with an ambiance, these keys of the ambiance are
  dropped and the stadium's laid over it; with no stadium (`none`) the ambiance plays alone, as written (an older
  pack's ambiance that hides the world still does). Names: lang `<namespace>.stadium.<id>`.
- `presets/<id>.json`: `{"stadium": "<id>", "ambiance": "<id>"}`, shown on top of the menu and usable as an ambiance
  id anywhere (an override naming a preset brings its stadium). Showtime's: `cosmos` (void), `ultra_space`
  (ultra_island), `champion` (arena), `grotto`, `crystal_grotto`, `dark_grotto` (cave), `dragon_lair` (volcanic_den), `open_sea`, `polluted_sea`,
  `frozen_sea` (sea), `deep_sea` (seabed), and one per League Reborn land or hall (`sunny_meadow`, `wildfire`,
  `snowy_peak`, `blackout`, `circus`...: the full list is `PRESETS` in `tools/stadiums.py`). The block palettes of
  the stadiums built of blocks are `BLOCKS` in the same script, laid over each stadium when it writes the files.
- `sea` (2026-11-19): the field on an islet (the real ground under the field, a sand beach, rocks on the shore), water
  out to `radius` rolling in waves of height `wave`; with `under`, the field on a sand seabed instead, the surface
  rippling `depth` blocks overhead, rocks and fish round it. Two stadiums use it: `sea` and `seabed` (a stadium of its
  own rather than a mode, so either place goes with any ambiance). Its anchors: the beach (or the seabed round the
  field) and the air.
- `land` (2026-11-19): an outdoor place out to `radius`, the real ground under the field, level for `flat` blocks,
  then `hills` high. `ground`: colours blended in noise patches; `grain`; `style`: `plain`, `dunes`, `summit` (the
  ground falls away into cliffs beyond the flat), `marsh`. Dressings, each optional: `ranges` (`color`, `snow`,
  `height`, `distance`, `layers`), `clouds` (a sea of clouds `depth` below: `color`, `shade`), `trees` (`kind`
  broadleaf / pine / dead, `count`, `ring`, `height`, `trunk`, `leaves`, `canopy`), `rocks` (`color`, `count`,
  `spires`, `ring`, `size`), `pools` (`color`, `rim`, `glow`, `count`, `ring`, `size`; the ambiance's `water.color`
  and `water.light` recolour them), `cracks` (`color`, `core`, `count`, `ring`), `columns` (`color`, `count`,
  `distance`, `height`, `ruined`), `junk` (`colors`, `count`, `ring`), `tiles` (2026-11-19: a pavement of `size`-block
  tiles on the world's grid out to `radius` blocks, 0 = the field and its `flat`; `joint` colour between tiles, each
  tile its own `shade`, `vein` for marble veins running across them; laid in blocks even when the ground is smooth).
  Every `ring` is in blocks past the field's edge.
- A `land` built of Minecraft's blocks (2026-11-19, the default ground look): the same place laid block by block
  (see "Grounds in blocks" below). Its blocks, each an id with optional properties (`oak_log[axis=x]`; an unknown id
  logs once and falls back): `blocks` (`surface`: the top, the first everywhere, the second and third in the patches
  the smooth ground colours with its second and third `ground` colours; `soil` under it; `rock` on cliffs and deeper,
  or `bands` of rock laid by height; `far`: the mountains' gentle tops, unset the first surface block), `plants` (a
  list of `{block, chance, ring}`: each grows on `chance` of the blocks that can hold it, within `ring` blocks of the
  centre, unset everywhere; double plants take both halves, cactus and sugar cane one to three high), `biome` (the
  biome whose colours tint grass, leaves and water; default `minecraft:plains`), `trees.species` (taken in turn:
  `oak`, `birch`, `spruce`, `dark_oak`, `jungle`, `acacia`, `cherry`, `azalea`, `dead`; unset: from `kind`),
  `rocks.blocks`, `pools.lilies` (0..1), `tiles.blocks` (one per tile), `columns.block` and `columns.capital`,
  `junk.blocks`. Pools are water, cracks lava over magma, `ranges` real mountains (snowed above 60 % of their height
  with `snow` or a snowy ambiance), `blaze` chars the trees and lights fires. The ambiance's `grass` and `flowers`
  become Minecraft's grass and flowers (a flower per colour, the nearest of Minecraft's). The sea of clouds stays
  drawn as before.
- A `sea` and a `cavern` built of blocks (2026-11-19, same setting): a sea's `blocks` (`surface` with its patches,
  `soil`, `rock`: the beach or seabed), `rock_blocks` (its rocks), `plants` (on the beach; under water seagrass, kelp,
  sea pickles, coral), `biome`; the water is Minecraft's, tinted with the ambiance's `water.color` (else the
  stadium's), ice when `frozen`, with snow and floes. A cavern's `blocks` (`surface` the floor, `rock` or `bands` the
  walls and vault), `pillar` (the pillars' block), `dripstone` (pointed dripstone hanging and rising, default true),
  `plants`; its lava lake is lava over magma, its field lit by hidden light blocks (as bright as its `light_strength`),
  the rest by little sky light (its `ambient`). Its `hoard` is blocks too (2026-11-20: piles of gold and raw gold
  blocks, gold plates for coins, the skeleton a fossil of bone blocks, sunk in the lava), and so are the ambiance's
  `stalactite` and `stalagmite` props on its vault and floor (pointed dripstone, long ones on dripstone blocks). The
  hoard's glints, the falls' glow and the ambiance's crystals stay drawn as before.
- `hall` (2026-11-19): a room `margin` blocks past the field, `height` high. `shape` `box` (walls, pilasters, beams,
  hanging lamps) or `tent` (round wall and cone in `stripes`). `floor`, `checker` + `tile` (a checkerboard), `wall`,
  `ceiling`, `lamp`, `mirrors`, `machines` (`metal`, `belt`, `crates`, `warning`, `gears`, `presses`, `speed`: a
  conveyor loop with crates, gears on the walls, presses), `pieces` (`white`, `black`, `count`: giant chess pieces,
  sized to the `tile`), `flat` (a level floor everywhere, even under the field). `mirrors` really reflect: the room
  and the entities in it are drawn again mirrored behind each wall, while the camera is inside the room and no shader
  pack is on (else a painted sheen). A wall the camera is outside of is not drawn.
- A `hall` built of blocks (2026-11-19, same setting): `floor_blocks` (the floor, the second block in patches),
  `checker_blocks` (the checkerboard's dark tiles, laid on the world's grid), `wall_blocks`, `ceiling_blocks`,
  `stripe_blocks` (a tent's wall and cone, by angle), `trim` (pilasters and beams), `lamp_block` (hanging on chains
  where the lamps glow; chains alone in a power cut), `mirror_block` (default `minecraft:glass`). The room is lit by
  hidden light blocks, dark in a power cut. A box hall with `mirrors` has glass walls with the room built again of
  blocks, mirrored, behind each wall and each corner; the people in it are drawn mirrored there, with or without a
  shader pack. Furnishings (2026-11-20, box halls): `wainscot` (a band `wainscot_height` high at the walls' foot,
  under the mirrors), `cornice` (a row of `trim` under the ceiling), `chandeliers` (rods of light round each lamp),
  `pedestal` (between each two pilasters) holding `wall_props` in turn, `carpet` (round the room, two blocks from the
  walls). Machines, chess pieces, cables and the glows stay drawn as before.
- Grounds in blocks (2026-11-19): every stadium's floor (land, islet, seabed, cave, hall without a checkerboard,
  Ultra Space's island) is drawn block by block on the world's grid by default, each top at a whole block, sides
  down to lower neighbours, still coloured per vertex; a seabed goes smooth past 48. A land is built of real blocks
  (above) out to the horizon: one block a block within 44 of the centre, 2-block cells to 84, 4-block cells beyond;
  the coloured one stands in while it is built (a second or two, in the background). Always: the smooth grounds and
  the setting that chose them were removed on 2026-11-20.
- Stands (`crowd`) stand level all round, at the field centre's height, whatever the blocks round the arena.
- An ambiance's `grass` (`colors`, `tip`, `count`, `ring` from the centre, `height`, `wind`) and `flowers` (`colors`,
  `count`, `ring`, `height`) grow on whatever floor the stadium gives (else the real ground). `blaze` (`color`,
  `core`, `flames`) sets a land on fire (trees and ground charred, flames in the crowns and round the field);
  `snow_cover` (0..1) snows a land in (ground, trees, rocks, ranges); `power_cut` (`color`, `cables`) stops a hall's
  machines, puts its lamps out, lights red emergency lamps and hangs sparking cables.
- An ambiance's `water`: `{color, deep, foam, waves, frozen, oil, clarity, light}`, every key optional: how it sees a
  `sea` stadium. `waves` multiplies the stadium's, `frozen` stills it into cracked ice with floes, `oil` lays rainbow
  slicks, `clarity` (0..1) sets the sun's glitter, `light` is the surface seen from below. Ignored without a sea.
- An ambiance's `light`: `{color, strength, rock, floor}`: the stadium's stone lit (and, with `rock`/`floor`,
  recoloured) by the ambiance.
- An ambiance's `props`: things it adds on surfaces round the field, never replacing a block. Each: `kind`
  (`crystal`, `stalactite`, `stalagmite`), `anchors` in order of preference (`ceiling`, `wall`, `floor`, `float`; what
  one kind lacks spills to the next, a prop with no kind available is left out), `count`, `size` [min, max],
  `color` (rock) or `colors` (crystals), `glow`, `pulse`, `wave`, `beams` (prism beams from ceiling or floating
  crystals), `grow` (ticks), `drips` and `drip` (water from stalactite tips). Anchors come from the stadium's vault
  when it has one, else from a scan of the real blocks: a cylinder `fieldRadius + 12` wide, from 2 blocks under the
  field to `ceiling_reach` above it (default 14, at most 32; a roof higher up is open sky), faces seen from the field,
  none in the field or within 2 blocks of a trainer. A stalactite never reaches lower than a third of the gap to the
  floor. A moment's `rockfall` drops that many rocks from the ceiling anchors (none under open sky).

### Transitions: `transitions/<from>_to_<to>.json` (2026-11-20, written by hand)

When the ambiance a mod imposes changes during a battle (a Pokémon Reborn field turning into another), a transition
of its own plays instead of the cut behind a flash: two or three seconds in which the place changes around the
battle. The new ambiance is in from the first tick; what of the old one the file names
stays a while to leave.

- `from`, `to`: ambiance ids (a preset counts for its ambiance; `*` for any). An exact pair wins over one with a `*`.
  Unqualified ids take the file's namespace: a file in another mod names Showtime's ambiances in full
  (`cobblemon_battle_showtime:cave`). Every namespace's `transitions/` folder is read.
- `camera` (optional; the second camera only): it pulls back from where it is, up and away, to circle the whole field
  for `seconds` (0: the transition's length), framing `reach` times the field's extent; other shots wait meanwhile, a
  knock-out alone cuts in. `shake`: how far it shakes at first, in blocks, dying out over `shake_seconds`.
- `ticks`: how long it plays. `blend`: ticks the sky, fog colour and fog distance take to turn from the old ambiance's
  into the new one's. `arrive`: ticks the new ambiance's mist takes to rise. `veins_fade`: ticks the old glowing veins
  take to die out, flickering (0: gone at once).
- `leaving`: the old props that stay to leave, by kind. `crystal`: `exit` `shatter` (each trembles and flares white
  for `flare` ticks, then breaks apart in `break_ticks`), one after another over `spread` ticks; when one breaks,
  `shard_count` shards of the block `shards` fly, a `sparkle` particle and its `sound` (`volume`) play. The old prism
  beams fade out in 12 ticks.
- `cues`: a timeline, each at its tick `at`: any moment key (`rockfall`, `particle`/`count`, `sound`/`volume`/`pitch`,
  `filter`/`filter_ticks`, `flash`…) plus `dust` (puffs of `dust_particle`, default `minecraft:large_smoke`, rising
  from the floor over the field and round it, as far as `dust_radius` times its extent, default 1.4), `debris` (bits of
  `debris_block` falling from above all over the field), `burst` (bits of `burst_block` blown out from the field's
  centre), `shake`/`shake_seconds` (a new jolt of the camera). The calm setting halves them and softens the shakes.
  `flash_ticks` holds the cue's `flash` that long (fading over its last 14 ticks), to hide a stadium being swapped.
- `cover` (optional, over a sea stadium's water): a sheet whose jagged front runs out from the field to `reach` blocks
  (0: the sea's reach) from tick `start` over `ticks`, patches of `colors` with a grain, a bright `edge` line, `alpha`.
  `mode` `spread`: the new look covers the old (the old water stays built under it until the front is out, then the
  sheet fades over `fade` ticks); `retreat`: the old look drawn back from the field over the new water.
- When both ambiances stand in the same stadium, its blocks stay until the new ambiance's are built.

## Trainer animations: `player_animations/*.json` (generated by `tools/trainer_animations.py`)

Player Animation Library's format (Emotecraft-compatible). Names are `<moment>_<style>`, moments: `guard`, `send_out` (the throw),
`recall`, `attack`, `victory`, `defeat`. Poses are in radians; `torso` moves the whole player (positive pitch tilts
backwards, positive y lifts); elbows and knees use `bend`.

## Screen filters: `shaders/` (generated by `tools/filters.py`)

Post-effect shaders used by ambiances (black and white, pixels, glitch, ripple, old TV): Minecraft 1.21.1 no longer
ships its own.

## Music (resource pack)

`assets/cobblemon_battle_showtime/sounds/music/<battle|victory|defeat>/*.ogg` (and `lobby`, once a mod turns it on), no declaration needed. The
older `assets/phantasmon/sounds/music/` is also read.
File names follow `<game>_<title>.ogg` (`oras_vs_wally.ogg`): `BattleMusic.title` shows it as "ORAS · Vs Wally"
(game codes in `BattleMusic.GAMES`); other names are shown as they are. `tools/music_names.py` renames downloaded
tracks to this convention (game acronym, then the title without "pokemon", "ost", quality tags or numbers). Template: `resourcepack-template/Cobblemon Battle Showtime Resource Pack`.

## Config

`config/cobblemon_battle_showtime.json`:

```json
{
  "ghost": { "stagedCamera": true, "intro": true, "music": true, "ballEffects": true },
  "pvp":   { "stagedCamera": true, "intro": true, "music": true, "ballEffects": true },
  "npc":   { "stagedCamera": true, "intro": true, "music": true, "ballEffects": true },
  "musicVolume": 1.0,
  "trainerProfile": { "guard": "guard_2" },
  "ambiance": "none",
  "checkUpdates": true,
  "cameraVersion": 0
}
```

`ghost` is the settings of battles staged through the API. `config/cobblemon_battle_showtime-music.json` holds the
unticked tracks (`disabled`), the favourites (`favorites`) and `onlyFavorites`;
`config/cobblemon_battle_showtime-intros.json` the same for the intros, by intro name. Both are written atomically; a missing or broken file means the defaults.

## Artwork (`art/`)

- `art/icons/`: sources of the official images, edited with Paint.NET (`.pdn`): the mod icon, the resource pack icon,
  the title banners and the Cobblemon logo used on them.
- `art/ambiances/` and `art/intros/`: the gallery, built by `tools/gallery.py` from in-game recordings: one
  screenshot and one 3-second clip each, and a looping crossfade reel (MP4 and GIFs).

Copies of the icons are shipped at 512 px:
`assets/cobblemon_battle_showtime/icon.png` and the template pack's `pack.png`. Regenerate them after editing a source.
